title: Client Rescue Sprint — Command Plan and Exec Escalation
content:
Purpose:
This document is a pragmatic, time-boxed command plan to convert a high-risk renewal into a retained customer within a 10-business-day rescue sprint. It combines rapid diagnosis, prioritized mitigation plays, an executive escalation play, and templated customer messaging so CS, SE, and GTM stakeholders can mobilize quickly.

Scope and when to use:
- Applies to enterprise and mid-market accounts flagged as: 1) Renewal < 60 days and at high churn risk, or 2) Major usage/quality regression detected and customer signals intent to pause/exit.
- Not for deals in early renewal cycles (<30 days since onboarding) where feature gaps are expected; use standard adoption playbooks instead.

Quick triage (first 24 hours):
1) Gather key facts (owner completes the Intake Snapshot): renewal date, ARR at risk, primary buyer(s), technical contact, most recent support and SRE incidents, last QBR notes, NPS/CSAT trends, active disputes, and open PRs/tickets impacting production.
2) Risk score (fast heuristic):
   - Financial exposure: 1-5
   - Technical severity: 1-5
   - Strategic importance: 1-5
   Aggregate >10 = high priority.
3) Assign a Rescue Lead (usually CSM) and Ops Lead (SRE/SE depending on issue).
4) Schedule day 1 customer sync (within 48 hours).

Escalation ladder (who to call):
- Tier 1 (Immediate): Rescue Lead (CSM), Solutions Engineer, Customer Success Manager Manager
- Tier 2 (Within 48 hours): Director of Customer Success, Product Manager owning the impacted feature
- Tier 3 (Within 72 hours): VP Customer Success, Head of Product, Head of Sales (if revenue commit at risk)
- Executive Bridge (triggered if contract value > $500k or unresolved after 5 days): CEO/COO standby + Legal + Security/Compliance for sensitive accounts.

Communication norms during a sprint:
- Daily internal standup: 15 minutes, share mitigation progress, blockers, and customer sentiment.
- Customer updates: cadence agreed on day 1 (every 48 hours minimum). If issue technical and customer-facing, provide a summary note with next action and ETA.
- All customer-facing commitments must be logged in Slack channel #rescue-<account> and in the account record (CRM).

Primary mitigation plays (pick based on root cause):
- Operational fixes (Low friction): patch config, change routing, increase quota limits, temporary feature toggles. Owner: SRE/SE. Timeline: 0–72 hours.
- Performance/backfill (Medium friction): allocate burst capacity on Dedicated, enable caching, tune batching/quantization profiles. Owner: Infra/Serving Runtime. Timeline: 24–96 hours.
- Model quality regression (High friction): roll back to previous model variant, enable fallback model, or deploy a targeted guardrail. Owner: Applied ML + Product. Timeline: 48–120 hours.
- Contract concessions (Commercial): short-term credit, extended payment terms, or pilot scoped for added value. Owner: AE/RevOps + CSM. Timeline: 24–72 hours.
- Compliance/legal remediation: expedite compliance review, provide SOC logs, or sign data processing addendum (DPA). Owner: Legal + Security. Timeline: variable but accelerate.

Rescue sprint phases and day-by-day checklist (10 business days recommended):
- Day 0 (Prep): Intake Snapshot complete, Rescue Lead assigned, internal notification sent, day 1 customer sync scheduled.
- Day 1: Customer sync — agree on objectives, success definition (what 'saved' looks like), and communication cadence. Create #rescue-<account> internal channel.
- Day 2–3: Rapid technical mitigations (Operational fixes). Track tickets, deploy quick patches, and validate.
- Day 4–6: Medium fixes and customer validation – performance adjustments, dedicated bursts, model/feature rollbacks if needed.
- Day 7–8: Commercial offers or contractual pauses if required; update execs if unresolved.
- Day 9: Final validation with customer, confirm usage/KPIs trending positive.
- Day 10: Closeout review: retention outcome captured, lessons, follow-up plan, and post-mortem scheduled.

Decision matrix (simple):
- If customer agrees to a 30-day pilot of a lowered-risk config and usage KPIs improve by 20% within 7 days → reduce escalation and propose renewal extension.
- If technical root cause cannot be mitigated within 5 days and value at risk > $250k → escalate to Executive Bridge.

Executive Bridge runbook (for when senior execs are engaged):
1) Briefing packet (one pager) — include: summary of the account, ARR at risk, top two technical issues, mitigation attempts and blockers, and requested executive ask (approval for extended credits, priority infra capacity, exceptions).
2) 30-minute executive sync with clear desired outcome: commit to resource (e.g., priority infra) or sign off for commercial concession.
3) Follow-up: exec-level note to customer within 24 hours confirming commitments and owner.

Customer messaging templates (short, adapt as needed):
- Day 1 sync invite (subject): "Rescue Sprint Kickoff — <Account> / Redwood Inference"
  Body (short): "Thanks for taking time. Our immediate objective is to stabilize X, validate Y, and ensure your team can continue planned workflows. Proposed agenda: 1) facts & impact 2) 48-hour mitigation plan 3) desired outcome. Please share any immediate constraints. — <CSM name>"

- Escalation to exec (to customer) (subject): "Executive follow-up — Redwood & <Account>"
  Body (short): "Our exec team is aligned and ready to support. We will be prioritizing capacity and product fixes over the next 72 hours. Can we align on a decision checkpoint on <date>? — <VP Customer Success>"

Metrics and tracker fields (to log in CRM or shared sheet):
- Account name, ARR at risk, Renewal date, Risk score, Rescue Lead, Ops Lead, Active mitigation plays, Tickets opened (IDs), Time to first mitigation (hours), Usage delta (% change), Customer sentiment (qualitative), Final outcome (retained, churned, at-risk extended).

Sample sprint tracker row (CSV-ready):
"Acme Corp","$420,000","2025-03-15","12","Asha Patel","Riley Nguyen","config-hotfix,dedicated-burst","TKT-9841;TKT-9850","6","+18%","tone: guarded -> hopeful","retained"

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Failure: slow cross-team approvals for infra bursts → Mitigation: pre-authorized emergency capacity for accounts over threshold; include finance SLA.
- Failure: insufficient telemetry to prove progress → Mitigation: require product teams to enable quick-scope dashboards or provide sample logs to customer.
- Failure: promises made without legal signoff → Mitigation: pre-approved concession templates and pricing guardrails.

Post-mortem template (to be completed 48–72 hours after sprint close):
- Outcome summary (one paragraph)
- Root cause (technical/operational/comms)
- What worked (list)
- What didn't work (list)
- Action items (owner + due date)
- Escalation policy changes recommended

Owner responsibilities (concise):
- Rescue Lead (CSM): single point of contact, runs day-to-day, drafts customer notes, owns CRM updates.
- Ops Lead (SE/SRE): accountable for technical mitigation and rollback decisions.
- AE/RevOps: negotiates commercial concessions and records changes to contract/renewal terms.
- Product/Applied ML: triage model/feature issues and supply rollback or patch plan.
- Legal/Security: expedite any compliance artifacts required by customer.

Checklist to close a sprint (minimum):
- Customer confirms resolution or agreed extension
- All mitigation tickets closed or in handover with SLAs
- CRM updated with final outcome and artifacts attached
- Post-mortem completed and shared with exec stakeholders
- If retained, schedule a health QBR within 30 days to rebuild confidence

Appendix: Example one-pager for Executive Bridge (copy/paste):
- Account: <Account Name>
- ARR at risk: <$$$>
- Renewal date: <date>
- 2-sentence summary: <what happened and current state>
- Top mitigations tried: <list>
- Blockers needing exec decision: <e.g., approve $X credit, allocate priority infra, sign exception>
- Desired outcome: <retain by X>

Notes and known constraints:
- This plan assumes cross-functional participants can commit to the 10-business-day cadence. If a critical approver is unavailable (e.g., legal holidays), adjust timelines and document the new checkpoint.
- Keep customer-facing messages concise and avoid promising permanent product changes; frame work as temporary stabilization followed by roadmap-driven fixes.

Version history:
- 2024-11-03 — draft created by Asha Patel
- 2024-12-15 — added Executive Bridge template (Priya Desai)
- 2025-02-20 — updated timing guidance and sample tracker (Liam O'Connor)

End of document.
